issues.description: SealSaloon.totalOrders is specified as an int in the UML, but implemented as a long in the reference solution. This causes a cross-artifact type mismatch for the field and its getter (getTotalOrders returns long), which can confuse students and break tests expecting an int-based counter.
issues.suggestedFix: Make totalOrders an int in SealSaloon and change getTotalOrders() to return int, or update the problem statement/UML to declare totalOrders (and the getter) as long consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement is internally inconsistent about SealSaloon.stock: it first describes it as an instance-level final field ("a final Stock stock"), but later explicitly requires stock to be static (shared across all instances). This ambiguity can mislead students about whether Stock is per-saloon or global.
issues.suggestedFix: Decide one design and make all artifacts consistent: either (a) update UML/text to clearly mark stock as static (e.g., {static}) and describe shared inventory, or (b) remove the static requirement and implement stock as a per-instance final field.

issues.description: Stock exposes a public mutator setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[]) in both template and solution, but the UML/spec does not include this method and frames Stock manipulation via addToStockIngredients/find/add/take/emptyStock plus getters. This extra setter can undermine the intended encapsulation and allow bypassing required logic.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove setStockIngredients(...) from template/solution if it is not intended for students, or explicitly add it to the UML/spec (e.g., marked as testing-only) so students know it is allowed.
